scheme_name: PMMSY: Fish Feed Plants of Production Capacity of at least 100 Ton/Day - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

This scheme aims to enhance fish production and promote sustainable fisheries in the country. 

The PMMSY is particularly significant for states like Haryana, which has a growing aquaculture sector. 

One of the key components of this scheme is the establishment of fish feed plants with a production capacity of at least 100 tons per day. 

The primary objective of this initiative is to increase the availability of quality fish feed. 

This is crucial for improving fish production and ensuring the sustainability of aquaculture practices. 

The scheme aims to achieve an increase in fish production to 22 million metric tons by 2024-2025. 

It also seeks to create an additional 55 lakh jobs in the fisheries sector by the same year. 

The PMMSY is expected to contribute to the doubling of the income of fishers and fish farmers. 

The financial outlay for the PMMSY is approximately INR 20,050 crores. 

This includes both central and state government contributions. 

For the fish feed plants specifically, the government provides a subsidy of up to 40% of the project cost. 

In the case of North Eastern states, this subsidy can go up to 60%. 

The establishment of fish feed plants is expected to reduce the dependency on imported fish feed. 

This will also help in stabilizing the prices of fish feed in the market. 

The eligibility criteria for setting up a fish feed plant under PMMSY include being a registered entity. 

This can be an individual entrepreneur, a cooperative society, or a company. 

The applicant must have a minimum educational qualification of 10th standard. 

Additionally, the applicant should have experience in aquaculture or related fields. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, the applicant must submit a detailed project report to the concerned fisheries department. 

This report should outline the proposed plant's capacity, technology, and operational plan. 

The applicant must also provide documents such as identity proof, address proof, and educational certificates. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the state fisheries department. 

If approved, the applicant will receive a sanction letter detailing the subsidy amount. 

The disbursement of the subsidy is typically made in installments. 

The first installment is released after the project is initiated. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the project. 

The timeline for establishing a fish feed plant can vary. 

However, it generally takes about 6 to 12 months from the date of project approval. 

The implementing authority for the PMMSY in Haryana is the Department of Fisheries, Haryana. 

This department is responsible for the overall implementation of the scheme. 

They provide technical support and guidance to applicants. 

The contact details for the Department of Fisheries, Haryana, can be found on their official website. 

The PMMSY also emphasizes the importance of technology in fish feed production. 

It encourages the use of modern techniques to enhance feed quality and reduce costs. 

The scheme promotes the establishment of feed plants in clusters to optimize resources. 

This clustering approach helps in better management and distribution of feed. 

The PMMSY also aims to promote research and development in fish feed formulations. 

This is essential for developing nutritionally balanced feeds that enhance fish growth. 

The scheme is aligned with the National Fisheries Policy, which aims to promote sustainable fisheries. 

It also supports the objectives of the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative by promoting self-reliance in fish production. 

The PMMSY is expected to have a significant impact on rural livelihoods. 

It will provide employment opportunities for local communities engaged in aquaculture. 

The establishment of fish feed plants will also lead to the creation of ancillary industries. 

These industries will provide raw materials and services to the fish farming sector. 

The scheme encourages the participation of women and marginalized communities. 

It aims to empower them by providing training and financial assistance. 

The PMMSY also focuses on promoting organic aquaculture practices. 

This is crucial for ensuring the sustainability of fish farming in the long term. 

The scheme includes provisions for capacity building and skill development. 

This will help fish farmers adopt modern practices and improve productivity. 

The PMMSY is a comprehensive initiative that addresses various challenges in the fisheries sector. 

It aims to create a robust ecosystem for fish production and processing. 

By enhancing fish feed production, the scheme will contribute to food security. 

It will also help in meeting the growing demand for fish in the domestic market. 

The PMMSY is a significant step towards achieving the goal of sustainable fisheries in India. 

It reflects the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of fishers and fish farmers. 

The establishment of fish feed plants under this scheme will play a crucial role in this endeavor. 

Overall, the PMMSY is a transformative initiative that has the potential to revolutionize the fisheries sector in Haryana and across India. 

The focus on quality fish feed production is expected to lead to increased fish yields and better economic returns for fish farmers. 

This scheme is an example of how targeted government interventions can drive growth in specific sectors. 

The PMMSY is set to create a sustainable and profitable fisheries sector in the country. 

This will ultimately benefit millions of people who depend on fishing for their livelihoods. 

The scheme's emphasis on technology and innovation will also pave the way for future advancements in aquaculture. 

In conclusion, the PMMSY's focus on fish feed plants is a crucial aspect of its broader objectives. 

It aims to enhance fish production and improve the overall health of the fisheries sector in India.
